issue_context.title: Home Assistant 2024.2.0 and greater Integration Traccar now sends Status / Location even if device offline
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Now that Traccar Integration is setup via UI it seems to get the device status from traccar AND proccessing it even if the device is offline.
Real World impact:
A person / account in HA has multiple device tracker (Mobile Companion App and Traccar).
Now the person.<name> gets updated with either location that was send last?!
Tracker B (Traccar) goes offline in City A. Person moves to City B, but the offline tracker stuck in City A with state offline still sends old coordinates and overwrites the more recent correct location. I debugged this shit like for 3 days now and finally found it is the traccar integration that behaves different than before.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.2.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2024.1.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

person

### Link to integration documentation on our website


### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I believe that this information is enough to recreate the issue. I checkt the mobile app logs, i checked the debug log of the mobile app, i checked location with the android device and everything was correct. In the DB i found that the only place where these gps coordinates originated from are traccar device_tracker. If you need anything else let me know.

This is not new behavior, offline devices was never discarded, as traccar still report it's last known location.
What did change was the move from legacy to standard tracking.
Maybe the person integration handles that differently.

Okay so should i move the issue to integration person?
I am a little lost here. Definitive a change in 2024.2.

Ill see if I can implement a limiter on the state writes. That's probably something that could be added regardless.
In an upcoming version I will move the position updates over to WebSocket, and there it would not be an issue anyway.
That has nothing to do with the issue described above.
You can allread get that with the custom attributes configuration options

> You can allread get that with the custom attributes configuration options

I have tried already but only items that are inside the traccar attributes element are working. 
I have tried with fixTime, deviceTime and serverTime, protocol without success. 
But all elements inside attributes worked.


just removed lat/lon from this sample from a request to traccar/api/positions

```json
{"id":2842283,"attributes":{"batteryLevel":68.0,"temp.ambient":27.0,"gear":"P","ignition":true,"ignitionState":"On","chargePortConnected":false,"charge":false,"power.mW":"913800.06","batteryLevel.wh":46240.0,"appVersion":"0.26.0.0010","distance":0.0,"totalDistance":1838677.54,"motion":false,"hours":121571571},"deviceId":135,"protocol":"carstatsviewer","serverTime":"2024-01-11T22:38:15.982+00:00","deviceTime":"2024-01-11T22:38:11.416+00:00","fixTime":"2024-01-11T22:38:11.416+00:00","outdated":false,"valid":true,"latitude":0.0,"longitude":0.0,"altitude":789.6577,"speed":0.0,"course":0.0,"address":null,"accuracy":0.0,"network":null,"geofenceIds":[112]}

```
Ah okay, my bad i thought you meant they where attributes

Not sure if my issue is about the same.
Please correct me.

Earlier, if the device is offline - it has a `status` attribute `unknown`.
Well, it is `unknown` now - but `last_changed` / `last_updated` are changing:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/7d9b4d63-08db-4c45-bd6b-4c5b7576f218)

In Traccar web interface the the device is offline:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/dea3527a-2b30-4d0a-bd54-40854cf40413)

Same in reports:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/9588c0e8-686c-49e6-aa54-c98afc65fab0)

How the `device_tracker` entity is considered as changed/updated if the device is offline?
Cannot provide proves now - but imho before `device_tracker` entity was not changing for offline devices.
Sorry if I am wrong.

And this is not related to the `person` entity.
The Traccar integration "marks" entities as "updated" - although they are NOT in fact.

Was it added to 2024.3?
I see no changes....

It is mentioned here:
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/0aa2fe61-ff69-43fb-8909-33a19c60b5a8)

But device_tracker still keep updating:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/9b9b7d6a-73bb-4500-98e3-82c832f227a5)

Polling is OFF, integration is updated in automation manually:

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/e57ab223-da38-419f-9d4c-5c0169a54780)

My expectation is: if attributes are not changed - the entity is NOT updated.

Switched ON polling again - and same behaviour.
I bet these same records are even written to DB ))))).

Guess I found a possible reason.
1. When polling is OFF & `device_tracker` entity is updated manually in automation by "update_entity" - the entity is always marked as "updated" - even if attributes are same.
My words above "Switched ON polling again - and same behaviour" were wrong: polling was switched ON, but automation still was ON as well.
So, a manual polling with "entity_update" marks an entity as "updated" - which is wrong since attrs are same.

2. When polling is ON, a `device_tracker` entity is not updated (as expected since attrs are same).

Seems that this option is wrongly named here as "polling":

![изображение](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/2c95ab90-f883-48be-93af-3fb525b168e1)

since the Traccar integration is not a "polling integration".
Means - a user cannot just switch off this "polling" & then update a `device_tracker` entity manually by "update_entity" - it may give wrong results described above.

review_comments: We should use `async_dispatcher_send` in async context.

It's possible to set coordinator data on a push event via:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/507384251429968ab2547aeed6786c33d6f0bac6/homeassistant/helpers/update_coordinator.py#L424
That will update all listeners which is one of the things i did not want to do as it causes additional state “updates”

Ok. Alternatively the coordinator supports adding a context when registering a listener which can be used to selectively update listeners. It's not without some extra code though. May not be worth it here.

Example:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/76784cbc957814efcf6761adc11cedcbb8e6dc4e/homeassistant/components/nibe_heatpump/coordinator.py#L32-L72
Ill take a look at that after I am finished splitting all attributes/events into their own entities.
If we're going to add event entities for the fetched events, I'd probably use a separate coordinator for that.
Events are a part of the websocket implementation, but it requires user configuration, so once moved to it it will be breaking

We could possibly use `hass.config_entries.async_create_background_task` here.

It will handle canceling the task on unload and shutdown.
Cool, did not know of that one, will give it a try.
These could be set outside of the constructor

They could, but they are instance attributes.
Why should they be set as class attributes?
Because they're initialized to a static value, but it was just a suggestion to make the constructor just a tiny bit cleaner

If they where truly static (does not change), or shared across all instances, I would agree.
But these are unique to each instance and do update during the lifecycle of that instance.
